headline: Record $15M Gift Fuels Cancer Research for Pets and People
meta_description: A couple donated a record $15 million to Virginia Tech's cancer center after the facility saved their cat from cancer, funding research to help both animals an…
summary_short: After Virginia Tech's cancer center saved their cat, a grateful couple made the largest gift in the center's history: $15 million for dual pet-human cancer research.
body:
A couple has given a record $15 million to Virginia Tech's cancer center after the facility successfully treated their cat for cancer. The donation is the largest gift in the center's history and will fund research aimed at helping both pets and people battling the disease.

The gift reflects a growing recognition that cancer research in animals and humans can advance together. By studying and treating cancer in companion animals like cats, researchers gain insights that can translate to human medicine—and vice versa. This couple's experience watching their own pet recover motivated them to invest in discoveries that could spare others from similar struggles.

Their generosity underscores how personal medical breakthroughs can inspire broader commitments to science. The Virginia Tech center now has unprecedented resources to pursue research that crosses the traditional boundary between veterinary and human oncology.
